stem.en: Put the long game in order, from a copying slip to a changed world.

text.en: DNA polymerase copies the tape by pairing and proofreads, leaving about one slip per billion letters.
Meiosis halves the chromosomes and shuffles them, and fertilisation joins two halves, so every seed is a new combination of spellings.
Alleles are spellings; some hide as recessives; their frequencies move with what they do in the world.
More are born than survive, the variation is inherited, and what survives becomes commoner: natural selection, with no chooser.
Separation and time pile up differences until populations cannot interbreed, and every species traces to one root.
Species live with partners, in webs where energy thins and atoms cycle, in biomes set by climate, on a planet whose air they have changed.
